title: 2002 HMMT February Guts Problem 1
statement: An \((l, a)\)-design of a set is a collection of subsets of that set such that each subset contains exactly \(l\) elements and that no two of the subsets share more than \(a\) elements. How many \((2,1)\)-designs are there of a set containing 8 elements?

solutions.text: There are \(\binom{8}{2}=28\) 2-element subsets. Any two distinct such subsets have at most 1 common element; hence, for each subset, we can decide independently whether or not it belongs to the design, and we thus obtain \(2^{28}\) designs.
